title: Daraxonrasib glues cyclophilin A to KRAS

provenance.note: KRAS G12D bound to GMPPNP, cyclophilin A and daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) from entry 9AX6, X-ray diffraction at 1.65 Angstrom, biological assembly 1. The coordinates are the prepared composite daraxonrasib-assembly-motion, built from its recipe: three chains named KRAS (with GMPPNP and magnesium), CYPA and DRUG. All three carry one shared rigid-body transform that turns the complex to face the opening view, so the composite at rest is the deposited arrangement. Waters are left out. In the first chapter the animation starts the drug and cyclophilin A away from their deposited positions and brings them back: the drug to cyclophilin A, then both to KRAS. That order follows the two binding steps measured in the primary citation (Jiang et al., Cancer Discovery 2024): daraxonrasib to cyclophilin A with a dissociation constant of 55 nM, then that binary complex to KRAS G12D with 364 nM. The starting positions and approach paths are illustrative; no intermediate is a measured structure. Switch I is drawn as residues 30 to 38 and switch II as residues 60 to 76. Contact counts and distances are measured from the deposited heavy atoms.

chapters.title: The glue assembles the complex
chapters.caption: Yellow daraxonrasib first binds purple cyclophilin A. That pair then binds teal KRAS on its two switch regions (coral). The order follows the two binding steps the authors measured. Where the pieces stop is the crystal structure 9AX6. Where they start and the paths they take are an illustration.

immersive.narration: The drug binds cyclophilin A, then the pair binds active KRAS. The paths are illustrative.

chapters.title: What the glue touches
chapters.caption: In 9AX6, 25 of the drug’s 58 non-hydrogen atoms lie within 4 Å of KRAS and 24 within 4 Å of cyclophilin A. Dashed lines mark two close contacts: 3.38 Å from a drug ring carbon to the ring of Tyr64 of KRAS switch II, a ring-to-ring contact, and 2.90 Å from the backbone nitrogen of cyclophilin A Asn102 to a drug carbonyl oxygen, with the distance and geometry of a hydrogen bond.

immersive.narration: The drug touches both proteins: Tyr64 of KRAS and Asn102 of cyclophilin A.

chapters.title: The complex, as measured
chapters.caption: The same complex drawn as ribbons: the deposited coordinates of entry 9AX6, from X-ray diffraction at 1.65 Å. KRAS G12D holds GMPPNP (grey), an analog of the GTP it carries when active. Cyclophilin A and the drug sit on switch I and switch II. The authors report that this complex blocks KRAS from binding its effectors.

immersive.narration: The measured complex: cyclophilin A and the drug cover the KRAS switches.

chapters.title: A small glue between two proteins
chapters.caption: The drug weighs 811 daltons. The two protein chains it joins in this crystal weigh about 19,400 and 18,100 daltons. In the headset, hold a grip and push the stick forward to enlarge the complex, then walk around it to find the drug between the two chains.

immersive.narration: A drug of 811 daltons joins two proteins. Hold a grip and push the stick forward to enlarge them.
